title: Powerful multiplicative groups do not force right nilpotence in finite braces
summary: For every odd prime $p$, we construct a finite left brace $A_p$ of order $p^{2p+1}$ whose additive group is elementary abelian and whose multiplicative group $G_p$ is a powerful $p$-group, but such that $A_p$ is not right nilpotent. More precisely, $G_p'=G_p^p\cong C_p^2, \operatorname{cl}(G_p)=2, \exp(G_p)=p^2,$ and $\operatorname{Soc}(A_p)=0$. Thus powerfulness does not force right nilpotence even for multiplicative groups of class two with derived subgroup of order $p^2$.
